items.claim: The row's second-person vocative unit (Isa.57.3-Isa.57.13) is a well-warranted, self-contained address with no undisclosed seam problem.
items.evidence: The fronted vocative pronoun opening “But draw near here, you sons of a sorceress” (web:Isa.57.3) carries a genuine tier-1 addressee shift away from the third-person meditation on the righteous perishing that precedes it, and the second-person indictment runs unbroken through the rhetorical challenge of Isa.57.11 to the antithetical refuge promise of Isa.57.13, the verse immediately before a fresh third-person messenger introduction opens at Isa.57.14. No petuchah/setumah break falls at either edge of the row's own span in the marks inventory, and the row correctly discloses that absence rather than staying silent on the layer. unit_type judgment_oracle and parent M7 Isa.56.1-Isa.66.24 both fit; the rejected rival (a sub-split at Isa.57.11) is a live, non-strawman possibility honestly disclosed.

items.claim: device_notes describes a distant verse comparison using the writer's own batch language rather than stating it purely by content, a register lapse.
items.evidence: device_notes calls the Isa.48.22 comparison "cross-part texture," language that names the writer's own batch structure rather than describing the two verses' relationship in Isaiah's own text; the same idea is fully expressible by content alone (a shared "no peace...for the wicked" saying that substitutes "my God" for the tetragrammaton at its close, correctly shown as a byte-level non-identity rather than a repeated refrain). The underlying boundary argument is otherwise sound: the messenger introduction at Isa.57.14, the high-and-lofty divine frame at Isa.57.15, and the postpositive amar-yhwh signature at Isa.57.19 are all byte-verified and correctly attributed to the divine (not royal-messenger) speech-frame class.

items.claim: device_notes twice identifies neighboring material by its position in the writer's row/part sequence rather than by verse content alone.
items.evidence: device_notes refers to Isa.56.2/Isa.56.4/Isa.56.6 as belonging to "this part's own opening row" and describes the Isa.57.21 mark disclosure as already given "at the prior row's close" - both phrases name the writer's own batching and row order rather than stating the cross-references purely by verse, which the cross-row-reference discipline (verse-anchored only) bars. The underlying boundary argument is otherwise sound: the imperative command-frame opening at Isa.58.1, the sustained question-and-answer fast oracle through Isa.58.6-Isa.58.12, and the closing divine-mouth-has-spoken formula at Isa.58.14 are byte-verified, and the sabbath-turn and then-pivot rivals at Isa.58.8/Isa.58.13 are honestly weighed rather than ignored.

items.claim: device_notes twice identifies neighboring rows by their position in the writer's sequence rather than by verse content alone.
items.evidence: device_notes states the Isa.58.14 mark was "disclosed already at the prior row's close" and that the closing argument "rests on the person shift that opens the next row at Isa.59.9, disclosed there as that row's own frame signal" - both phrases name row order in the writer's own sequence rather than the verses' place in Isaiah's text, which the cross-row-reference discipline bars. The underlying boundary argument is otherwise sound: the fresh assertion opening Isa.59.1 that answers the prior oracle's closing formula, the sustained second-person indictment through Isa.59.3, and the honest, undecided disclosure of the person-shift rival at Isa.59.4 are all well-grounded.

items.claim: The row's voice-shift argument for Isa.59.9-Isa.59.14 is byte-verified and its own tag imprecision is honestly disclosed rather than papered over.
items.evidence: The row's claim that the unit opens on a person shift into first-person-plural confession forms running unbroken to Isa.59.14 holds against the text, and device_notes candidly flags that its own addressee-shift tag names the nearest available taxonomy class for what is actually a grammatical person/voice shift rather than a true addressee change - exactly the kind of one-sentence deviation disclosure the operative-category rule calls for. The claim that Isa.59.15's own first clause is grammatically part of the wayyiqtol narrative chain that follows (rather than the confession that precedes it) is byte-verified: the verse opens with a vav-consecutive (wayyiqtol) verb form, matching the same chain-initial verb form as the wayyiqtol pair that immediately follows it in the same verse. The disclosed rival (attaching Isa.59.15's first clause to this row instead) is a genuine, non-strawman possibility.

items.claim: boundary_rationale identifies the row's own closing verse by its position in the writer's assigned batch rather than by its place in Isaiah's own text.
items.evidence: boundary_rationale states that the row "closes the part at web:Isa.59.21, its assigned range's final verse" - naming a writer-assignment boundary rather than a literary one (Isaiah's own text runs on into Isa.60.1 without any frame break at the 59:21|60:1 join that this row could claim as its own). The underlying boundary argument for holding Isa.59.15-Isa.59.21 together is otherwise sound and byte-verified: the wayyiqtol narrative chain opening at Isa.59.15, the postpositive-signature close of the Redeemer-arrival oracle at Isa.59.20, and the continuing first-person divine speech of the covenant formula at Isa.59.21 (marked twice by the amar-yhwh signature, both instances byte-confirmed) support keeping the covenant formula with the oracle rather than splitting it off.

items.claim: A confidence of high on a span that is exactly one whole chapter (Isa.60.1-Isa.60.22, all 22 verses) violates the calibration discipline capping whole-chapter spans at medium_low, and a digit-bearing title-count claim in device_notes is wrong against its own inventory.
items.evidence: The row's span is the entirety of Isa 60 (verse 1 through the chapter's last verse, 22), which the calibration rule for whole-chapter spans requires to sit no higher than medium_low regardless of how well-marked the internal address is; a confidence of high is an unexamined overreach on a chapter-scale unit. Separately, device_notes describes the qadosh-Israel construct recurring at Isa.60.9 and Isa.60.14 as belonging to a 24-verse signature title spanning both halves of the book - the title's own byte-swept count is 25 verses (12 in chs 1-39, 13 in chs 40-66), so the digit attached to this named object is one short of its actual count. The seam argument itself (the second-person-feminine-singular imperative address opening at Isa.60.1, sustained through the recognition-formula echo at Isa.60.16 and Isa.60.22, closing before the new first-person prophetic-commission frame at Isa.61.1) is otherwise well-grounded and correctly disclosed against the setumah marks at both of its edges.
